title: Anthropic's Next AI Infers Vague Intent for October Release
summary:
The San Francisco AI lab is developing a model that can identify a broad class of software bugs after being tasked with fixing only one, The Information reports. The unreleased system is designed to deduce a user's underlying objectives when instructions are imprecise and to solve problems more creatively than existing commercial models. It is expected to launch in October, coinciding with the release of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and a new Terra model from OpenAI.

The reporting follows leaks of a 'Fable 5.5' model in Microsoft Azure and LiteLLM's GitHub data. Traces of a model named 'claude-onigiri-eap-2' also appeared in Artificial Analysis's code, featuring four distinct reasoning levels from low to 'xhigh.' While Anthropic has not officially announced a date, several sources indicate corporate partners have already tested two separate checkpoints of the Fable 5.5 model.

selectedTweets.text:
An unreleased Claude model has surfaced in Artificial Analysis's website code. Spotted by Lumina, "claude-onigiri-eap-2" appears with four reasoning levels: low, medium, high and xhigh, plus an Opus 4.8 fallback.

Separately, leaker Lyra claims Anthropic's partners already have access to Fable 5.5 for testing. That could point to an approaching release, but Anthropic hasn't announced anything. Whether Onigiri is actually Fable 5.5 remains unconfirmed, and the suggested launch dates are guesses.
